svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Light-dependent reactions, on the thylakoid membranes: light is absorbed by chlorophyll in photosystem II, exciting electrons."], [2, "Photolysis: water is split, 2H\u2082O \u2192 O\u2082 + 4H\u207a + 4e\u207b. The electrons replace those lost from PSII; oxygen is given off."], [4, "Electrons pass along carriers to photosystem I. The energy released pumps H\u207a into the thylakoid space."], [6.5, "Light re-excites the electrons at PSI. They pass via ferredoxin to NADP reductase: NADP\u207a + H\u207a \u2192 NADPH."], [9, "Chemiosmosis: H\u207a flow back into the stroma through ATP synthase, which makes ATP (photophosphorylation)."], [12, "ATP and NADPH move into the stroma for the light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle)."], [13, "Carbon fixation: rubisco joins CO\u2082 to RuBP (5C); the product splits into two glycerate 3-phosphate (GP, 3C)."], [15.5, "Reduction: GP is reduced to triose phosphate (TP, 3C), using ATP and NADPH."], [17.5, "Some TP leaves the cycle to make glucose, sucrose, starch, amino acids and lipids."], [19, "Regeneration: the rest of the TP is used to make RuBP again, using ATP. The cycle continues."]]
svg.title: Chloroplast and photosynthesis
svg.desc: A chloroplast with double membrane, stroma, grana of thylakoids, lamellae, starch, lipid droplets, ribosomes and DNA, with insets of the light-dependent reactions on the thylakoid membrane and the Calvin cycle in the stroma.
svg.text: Chloroplast drawn as in an electron micrograph (about 5 µm long). Insets much enlarged.

g.data-info: The chloroplast has a double membrane (envelope): outer and inner.
Inner membrane of the envelope; controls what enters and leaves the stroma.
Fluid round the thylakoids: the light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) happen here, with the enzyme rubisco.
A thylakoid membrane joining one granum to another.
A stack of thylakoids: a large surface area of membrane for light absorption.
Flattened membrane sac containing chlorophyll in photosystems. The light-dependent reactions happen on its membrane.
Stored carbohydrate made from the products of the Calvin cycle.
Small ribosomes like those of bacteria (evidence for endosymbiosis).
Naked circular DNA, like a bacterium’s (evidence for endosymbiosis).
Chlorophyll and pigments absorb light; excited electrons leave. They are replaced by electrons from the photolysis of water.
Plastoquinone, cytochrome b6f and plastocyanin pass electrons from PSII to PSI. Cytochrome b6f uses the energy to pump H⁺ into the thylakoid space.
Light re-excites the electrons, which pass via ferredoxin to NADP reductase.
Reduces NADP⁺ to NADPH, using the electrons and H⁺ from the stroma.
H⁺ flow from the thylakoid space back into the stroma through ATP synthase, which makes ATP (photophosphorylation).
2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. Oxygen is the waste product; the H⁺ adds to the gradient.
Light-independent reactions in the stroma: carbon fixation, reduction of GP to TP using ATP and NADPH, and regeneration of RuBP.
Enzyme that fixes CO₂ by joining it to RuBP (5C); the 6C product splits at once into two GP (3C).
